articles.title: Repairing Crashed Database Tables in WordPress
articles.excerpt: WordPress is a database heavy application, especially for sites that use too many plugins (in my opinion). I’ve come across the following database error while working with WordPress numerous times: Ta…
articles.body: WordPress is a database heavy application, especially for sites that use too many plugins (in my opinion). I’ve come across the following database error while working with WordPress numerous times: Table `wp_*.wp_posts` is marked as crashed and should be repaired It’s easy to fix when you know what typically causes it, and how to repair your database tables. Here’s an overview based on what I’ve found from dealing with it myself numerous times. Common Causes Out of Disk Space The most common cause is an exhausted server, or more specifically: you’re probably out of disk space on the server running MySQL. MySQL typically limits the space available for database storage to the space on your disk, but it depends on the my.cnf configuration settings you have in place.

articles.body: Detecting sophisticated Android spyware is difficult, especially for people without access to a computer or technical security tools. That's why I'm developing Spyhound. It's a free, open-source Android application that checks devices for published indicators associated with spyware and stalkerware. What makes Spyhound different? Runs directly on Android Performs scans offline Doesn't require a computer for basic scanning Supports deeper inspection through Shizuku or root Explains findings, suspicious indicators and detection gaps Includes no advertising or user tracking Provides reproducible Android builds Transparency matters Spyhound cannot guarantee that a device is clean. articles.title: llms.txt validator: the 8 format mistakes we see, and a free tool to catch them
articles.excerpt: We check /llms.txt on every site our auditor scans, and most files that exist fail on format, not on content. So we put the same checks in a free page: fill in a few fields to generate a file, or past…
articles.body: We check /llms.txt on every site our auditor scans, and most files that exist fail on format, not on content. So we put the same checks in a free page: fill in a few fields to generate a file, or paste yours to validate it. It runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere. Tool: llms.txt generator and validator (also in Spanish ) The format in one minute The proposal at llmstxt.org defines the parts in this order. Only the first is required. An H1 with the site name: # Example Store A blockquote summary: > Example Store sells handmade ceramics... Optional paragraphs or lists, no headings H2 sections, each a list of links: - [name](url): notes One section can be called ## Optional for links an agent may skip when it needs a shorter context.

articles.title: Most Common Cause of a Slow WordPress Admin
articles.excerpt: A slow WordPress admin is the worst, it can significantly reduce publishing productivity, and it’s a big pain for anyone that works in the admin frequently. It can be caused by many things, but the mo…
articles.body: A slow WordPress admin is the worst, it can significantly reduce publishing productivity, and it’s a big pain for anyone that works in the admin frequently. It can be caused by many things, but the most common and least discussed seems to be slow HTTP API responses from premium or paid plugins that require a license key. When your site has paid or premium plugins that require a license and a very slow admin, the API calls made by these plugins are most likely the source of the problem. Both free and premium plugins make API requests, but free ones make all of their requests to api.wordpress.org, which is built to handle an extremely high volume of traffic.

articles.body: NASA's Artemis IV moon mission will be a complicated affair — especially if SpaceX's Starship ends up being the lunar lander. For all of the changing components of the Artemis program over the past several years, one of its most persistent may be the question of how many refueling flights Starship will need to land astronauts on the moon . By summer 2021, it was common knowledge that Starship would require multiple launches to pull off an Artemis moon landing. A Government Accountability Office audit at the time, for example, estimated that it could take up to 16. Earlier this month, a member of the Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel said the refueling number could be as high as 22.
